Sergio / Grace — forwarding technical notes I prepared for Finova. Oliver, adding this here so procurement has it in-thread. Short summary first, then the notes: 

Summary (quick bullets you can paste into the procurement packet):
- Batching: continuous batching on typical Finova request profiles yields ~8–18% token cost reduction while preserving 95th%-tile latency targets for interactive paths. Benefit scales with concurrency.
- KV/Prefix caching: for coherent session workloads (chatflows, customer-states) caching can reduce compute tokens by 12–40% on cached prefixes; depends heavily on repetitiveness of prompts.
- Quantization: for LLaMA-like 13B models we recommend starting with INT8/Naive Q4 (quantize weights + MHA-friendly kernels) in staging. Expected perf: ~30–45% reduction in memory and 10–30% lower token-costs depending on kernel support. For 7B, Q4_0 or INT8 often gives comparable accuracy with larger relative cost reductions.
- Additivity: batching + caching are largely additive (batching reduces per-token compute, caching reduces token count). Quantization reduces runtime cost per token; in practical workloads expect diminishing returns — combined uplift cap typically in the 40–65% range depending on overlap.

Technical notes (more detail you can attach to the RFP):
1) Measurement baseline: run a 2-week profiler using production-like sequences (we recommend 1k sessions with 90/10 short/long split). The profiler outputs per-route sequence distribution that drives batching kernel selection.
2) Canary plan: deploy quantized variant behind canary policy (5–10% of traffic) with automatic rollback on perplexity/regression alerts we instrument.
3) Implementation: we provide quantization recipes + kernel selection guidance. For MHA-heavy layers use kernel fallback: Fast-MHA (FP16) -> INT8-MHA (if available) -> fallback.
4) Expected savings model: we deliver a CSV with modeled token-savings by route (attached).

Attachment: quantization-estimates.csv (CSV, 12KB)
Attachment: optimize-playbook.pdf (PDF, 1.1MB)
